findings.message: check_connections assigns `missing="$(jq ...)"` without checking jq's exit status. If the REST body is not valid JSON, jq fails, `missing` stays empty and the function prints `ok service-connections: ready`. check_pipeline has the opposite flaw: a jq failure falls through to `missing pipeline`, which reports 'could not ask' as 'not found'. Both must return 2 (skip) when the response does not parse, for example by wrapping the jq calls in `|| { echo skip ...; return 2; }` and requiring `.value` to be an array.
findings.scenario: AZDO_TOKEN is expired or invalid and dev.azure.com answers 203 with an HTML sign-in page. `curl -sf` treats 203 as success, jq fails to parse the body, and doctor prints `ok service-connections: ready` (exit 0) although nothing was checked. The same response makes check_pipeline print `missing pipeline`. The ac16 AZDO_DOWN row only covers a curl exit of 22, not a 2xx with a non-JSON body.

findings.message: Doctor now reads `fleet.kube_connection` and `fleet.azure_connection` from config (README example: `specclaw-fleet-hetzner`). Both pipeline templates still hardcode `fleetKubeConnection: specclaw-fleet-k3s` and `fleetAzureConnection`. The same setting now exists twice and the copies can disagree. Either drop the config keys for the connections, or generate the template from config, or make doctor check the names the template really uses.
findings.scenario: Config has `kube_connection: specclaw-fleet-hetzner` and that connection is ready, so doctor prints `ok service-connections`. The checked-in pipeline still uses `specclaw-fleet-k3s`, which does not exist, so the pipeline run fails at the kube login step.

findings.message: The pipeline clears `FLEET_KUBE_CONTEXT` so a local config value cannot redirect the hosted run. The sibling local-only setting `kubeconfig` (exported as `KUBECONFIG` from config, README says local commands) is not cleared in either template, and ac22 only tests the context. The fix covers one spelling of the class 'local cluster pointer from config'.
findings.scenario: Config has `kubeconfig: /Users/me/.kube/hetzner` and the pipeline agent does not pre-set KUBECONFIG. `load_fleet_settings` exports that path on the agent, kubectl reads a file that does not exist, and dispatch fails or targets the wrong cluster.

findings.message: The diff changes code under plugins/specclaw-fleet and plugins/specclaw-sync (new commands, a new azdo-issue subcommand, pipeline and image prompt changes) but touches no plugin.json or marketplace.json version. The README now references image 0.9.0. Bump every `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, every `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` and every `plugins[]` entry in marketplace.json to the same new version.
findings.scenario: A user who has the previous version installed does not get the new optin/status commands or the new fleet: settings, because the plugin version did not change.

findings.message: The `[A-Za-z0-9+/_-]{52,}` heuristic matches any long path or name made only of those characters, for example a kubeconfig path. Every fleet command then dies with 'looks like a secret'. Exempt values for path-typed keys, or require the value to contain no `/` separators beyond a leading one.
findings.scenario: `kubeconfig: /home/ops/clusters/production-eu-west/kubeconfigs/specclaw-fleet-prod` has no dots or colons and is over 52 characters, so every specclaw-fleet command is refused.
